limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses gnotobiotic mice with a defined bacterial consortium (Oligo-MM12), which may not fully represent the complexity of the natural gut microbiome.
Sex-specific effects were observed, but the study may not be powered to fully dissect sex differences.
The study does not include a rescue experiment to confirm causality of fungal effects via immune modulation.

experiments_or_tasks: Gnotobiotic mice colonized with Oligo-MM12 bacteria alone (B) or with one of three fungal species (B+C, B+R, B+M) were fed standard diet (SD) or high-fat-high-sucrose (HFHS) diet. Metabolic health was assessed via body weight, body composition (TD-NMR), adipocyte size, oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), plasma lipids, and metabolic hormones.

methods.name: Gnotobiotic mouse model
methods.protocol_description: Germ-free C57BL/6 mice were colonized at weaning with Oligo-MM12 bacterial consortium alone (B) or with addition of Rhodotorula mucilaginosa (B+R), Malassezia restricta (B+M), or Candida albicans (B+C). Mice were fed standard diet (SD) or high-fat-high-sucrose (HFHS) diet for 12 weeks.

methods.name: Body composition measurement
methods.protocol_description: Time-domain nuclear magnetic resonance (TD-NMR) was used to measure fat and lean mass.

methods.name: Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT)
methods.protocol_description: After 6 h fasting, mice were gavaged with 50% dextrose (2 g/kg body weight) and blood glucose measured at 0, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120 min.

methods.name: Adipose tissue histology
methods.protocol_description: Peri-gonadal adipose tissue was fixed, paraffin-embedded, sectioned at 4 μm, H&E stained, and adipocyte size quantified using Adiposoft plugin in ImageJ.
